prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: EN · Plan comparison (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Feature" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 93px
  col 2: header "Free" · longest unbreakable word 88px · one-line width 88px
  col 3: header "Pro" · longest unbreakable word 73px · one-line width 73px
  col 4: header "Enterprise" · longest unbreakable word 83px · one-line width 255px
  col 5: header "Notes" · longest unbreakable word 81px · one-line width 465px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 643px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 642px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare Free, Pro, and Enterprise plan capabilities feature by feature, with Notes supplying caveats and context.","reading":"Readers scan down the Feature labels, then compare across the three plan columns; Notes is read afterward as supporting detail.","groups":["Free, Pro, and Enterprise belong together as parallel plan-value columns and should remain easy to compare.","Feature is the row-label column and anchors each comparison.","Notes is a separate explanatory column and should not compete with the plan values."],"keep_intact":["Headers: Feature, Free, Pro, Enterprise, Notes","Short plan values such as Unlimited, Community, 30 days, 1 year, and Custom","Tokens such as SSO / SAML and 24/7","Numeric units such as 2 GB and 100 GB"],"may_wrap":["Notes prose","The long Enterprise support phrase at word boundaries","Multi-word Feature labels if necessary"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [112, 112, 104, 150, 163] · table 642×501px · row heights [39, 92, 92, 118, 39, 118] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [104, 112, 100, 116, 209] · table 642×422px · row heights [39, 66, 92, 92, 39, 92] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [150, 110, 100, 110, 171] · table 642×501px · row heights [39, 92, 92, 118, 39, 118] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
